cyclisation: Reported as a selection-based macrocyclic library. The released sequences give the randomised region in single-letter code only; the cyclisation chemistry and any initiator are not encoded in the released file and must not be inferred from it.
noncanonical: Not represented in the released sequences, which use the 20 canonical letters. Non-canonical content of the underlying library is not recoverable from this file.
feature_encoding: categorical symbol at each randomised position, vocabulary read from the library itself
endpoint: selection enrichment from the focused library
direction: higher is better; enrichment is not affinity, inhibition or antiviral activity
censoring: Half the library sits at exactly 0.0 (9,192 of 18,429). These are non-enriched members, not measurements of zero affinity, and the bottom of the range is therefore censored rather than resolved.
rationale: 18,429 unique 12-mer members with 18,364 of them carrying more than one substitution from the consensus, so it is combinatorial at landscape scale rather than a single-substitution scan. It is the first substrate in this project drawn from an actual display selection against a real target. In-pool surrogate Spearman at 128 labels is 0.55, inside the learnable band identified in the coverage work.
source: Zhai et al., PepExplainer: an explainable deep learning model for selection-based macrocyclic peptide bioactivity prediction and optimization, Eur J Med Chem 2024;275:116628, doi:10.1016/j.ejmech.2024.116524. Data file taken from the authors' code repository, github.com/zhaisilong/PepExplainer (MIT licence), retrieved 20 October 2026.
limitations: These libraries were released as part of a published model's code repository. They are secondary distributions, not the original measurements, and no replicate structure, assay protocol or measurement error is available for any of them.
Enrichment, bioactivity and reported activity are three different endpoints on two different targets. Metrics are never pooled across these landscapes.
None of these is a pathogen target. They are substrates for developing and testing binding prediction on the correct molecule class, and establish nothing about Coronaviridae or Orthomyxoviridae.
No result from these landscapes speaks to the SynX platform's own chemistry, which remains blocked on the campaign export.
Enrichment from a focused library reflects that library's composition and the selection conditions. It is not a population-wide measurement and does not transfer to a naive library.
The consensus sequence is a statistical mode over the released members, not a declared wild type.
